decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's established airfield-lighting systems, it likely meets strategic aspirations and can be supported by current organizational slack.
The surveillance display fits the firm's integrated airport-operations portfolio, so absent clear failure management would more likely retain it than reallocate resources.
Training programs are close to the firm's service base and help support installed systems, so satisfactory if modest results would usually justify keeping it.
This narrower training course appears less strategically central and easier to discontinue if results fall short of aspiration or are absorbed into broader training offers.

Collaboration software directly matches the firm's stated direction toward integrated, real-time and collaborative airport operations, which raises the aspiration to continue developing it rather than exit.

Because it was presented as a flagship surveillance product aligned with the firm's future direction, behavioral theory implies management would be reluctant to drop it unless performance were clearly unsatisfactory.
